items.title: central boiler plant performance
items.text:
Space heating is provided by {number} {condensing/non-condensing} boilers rated at {capacity} MBH each, installed circa {year}.

While the boilers are in {condition} mechanical condition, observed operating temperatures of approximately {supply}/{return}°F limit sustained condensing operation.

Analysis indicates that heating energy intensity is approximately {percentage}% higher than benchmark values, primarily driven by elevated supply temperatures and limited temperature reset control.

Opportunities exist to improve seasonal efficiency through hydronic balancing, optimized temperature reset strategies, and enhanced control sequencing.

items.title: domestic hot water performance
items.text:
Domestic hot water is generated by {number} {boiler type} boilers serving {number} storage tanks.

The system operates at a storage temperature of approximately {storage_temp}°F with mixing valve delivery at {mix_temp}°F.

Although the system is operationally stable, analysis indicates {issue if applicable: high recirculation losses / storage oversizing / peak demand deficiency}.

Targeted optimization of storage strategy, recirculation control, and temperature monitoring presents opportunities to reduce energy use while maintaining occupant comfort.

items.title: central cooling plant performance
items.text:
Cooling is provided by a {chiller/WSHP/fluid cooler} system installed circa {year}.

The plant is mechanically functional; however, cooling-related energy consumption is primarily influenced by operational control strategies rather than equipment condition.

Enhanced BAS integration, temperature reset optimization, and improved sequencing could reduce peak electrical demand and seasonal consumption.

items.title: make-up air operational performance
items.text:
Ventilation is provided via {number} make-up air units equipped with {gas-fired/hydronic/DX} heating and {VFD/non-VFD} supply fans.

Current operation lacks {occupancy-based modulation / BAS coordination / airflow reset}, resulting in elevated heating demand during part-load conditions.

Control optimization and airflow modulation represent near-term opportunities for measurable energy savings.

items.title: absence or limitation of BAS
items.text:
The absence (or limitation) of a centralized Building Automation System (BAS) represents the primary operational constraint identified in this audit.

Implementation of BAS-driven temperature reset, scheduling, and coordinated system control is expected to yield the most significant near-term energy savings and operational improvements.
